hxfilelist.h File Reference

Detailed Description

This file contains definitions for the Hx UI Toolkit filelist API. The filelist widget is used by the File dialogs and File Manager application. It is an extended list that displays the contents of a directory.

HxResult HxFileListDelete ( HxFileList_t *  pFileList  ) 

Delete a file list widget.

HxFileListDelete deletes a file list created from an earlier call to HxFileListNew.

It is not necessary to call this function when quitting the application, since the widget's parent calls this function just before the parent is deleted. HxFileListDelete only needs to be called when removing a list at runtime.

Parameters:
pFileList IN: Pointer to the list to delete
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

HxResult HxFileListGetPath ( HxFileList_t *  pFileList,
char *  pPath,
int32_t *  pBytes 
)

Get the current directory.

This function returns the current directory.

If pFilename is set to NULL, *pBytes is set to the size of the buffer required, and HX_OK is returned.

Parameters:
pFileList IN: Pointer to file list
pPath IN: Pointer to the buffer path buffer, or NULL
pBytes IN/OUT: Pointer to the size of the path buffer. If buffer is too small, the required buffer size is returned
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK on success. Returns HX_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL if buffer is not large enough for file name.

HxResult HxFileListGetSelection ( HxFileList_t *  pFileList,
int32_t  index,
char *  pFilename,
int32_t *  pBytes,
bool *  pIsDirectory 
)

Get the selected filename.

HxListGetSelection returns the selected filename, and whether the selection is a directory.

The index is based on the count returned by HxFileListGetSelectionCount. For example, if HxFileListGetSelectionCount returns a count of 2, index 0 returns the first selected file, while index 1 returns the second selected file.

The application should set *pBytes to the size of the buffer passed. If *pBytes is less than the size required, HX_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL is returned, and *pBytes is set to the size of the buffer required.

If pFilename is set to NULL, *pBytes is set to the size of the buffer required, and HX_OK is returned.

Parameters:
pFileList IN: Pointer to file list
index IN: Index of the selected item to return
pFilename IN: Buffer for the filename string, or NULL
pBytes IN/OUT: Pointer to the size of the character buffer. If buffer is too small returns the required minimum buffer size
pIsDirectory OUT: Boolean flag set to true if returned filename is a directory; can be set to NULL
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK on success. Returns HX_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL if buffer is not large enough for file name.

HxResult HxFileListGetTopVisible ( HxFileList_t *  pFileList,
char *  pFilename,
int32_t *  pBytes,
int64_t *  pSize,
time_t *  pDate,
bool *  pIsDir 
)

Get the first visible file.

Gets the first visible file in the file list with all the data necessary to place it correctly independent of the sorting order.

pFile, pSize, pData, or pIsDir can be set to NULL if the caller does not care about that parameter.

pBytes must not be NULL. If pFile is set to NULL, or if *pBytes <= 0, then the number of characters in the top visible filename is returned in pBytes, and HX_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL is returned.

Parameters:
pFileList IN: Pointer to file list
pFilename OUT: Pointer to the filename, or NULL
pBytes IN/OUT: Pointer to the size of pFile buffer
pSize OUT: Pointer to the size of the file, or NULL
pDate OUT: Pointer to the modification date, or NULL
pIsDir OUT: Set to true if top item is a directory, or NULL
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK on success. Returns HX_NOT_FOUND if the file list is empty.

HxResult HxFileListSetFileAttributes ( HxFileList_t *  pFileList,
HxFileListFilleAttributes_t  attributes,
const char *  pFile 
)

Set the attributes of a file.

HxFileListSetFileAttributes allows the application to control the behavior of a file list after it is created.

The pFile argument allows the application to control while file list entry should be drawn with the kHxFileListGrayedOut attribute. Note that all other flags in the attributes argument must be set correctly when setting a file's grayed-out attribute.

Parameters:
pFileList IN: Pointer to file list
attributes IN: File list attributes
pFile IN: Pointer to filename for kHxFileListGrayedOut
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK on success.

HxResult HxFileListSetFilter ( HxFileList_t *  pFileList,
HxFileFilter  filter,
void *  pContext 
)

Set the file filter for the file list.

HxFileListSetFilter sets the file filter used by the file list when displaying a list of files. The filter is called when the files in a directory are scanned, and allows an application to display a subset of all of the files in the directory.

Parameters:
pFileList IN: Pointer to file list
filter IN: File filter function
pContext IN: User data passed as first parameter to filter
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK on success. Returns HX_INVALID_ARG if the dialog is not the file dialog.

HxResult HxFileListSetPath ( HxFileList_t *  pFileList,
const char *  pPath 
)

Set the file path.

If pPath is set to a directory, the first file visible in the file list is selected. If pPath is set to a file, that file is marked selected.

Parameters:
pFileList IN: Pointer to file list
pPath IN: Pointer to path
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK on success. Returns HX_MISSING_FILE if path is invalid.

HxResult HxFileListSetSelection ( HxFileList_t *  pFileList,
HxFileListSelectionAttributes_t  attribute,
const char *  pFilename 
)

Set the selected filename.

This function marks a file in the filelist as selected, and causes it to be drawn with the highlighted color.

The attribute parameter controls how files are selected. If attributes is set to kHxFileListOneSelected, then pFile is selected after clearing the selection of any other file marked selected in the list. If attributes is set to kHxFileListMultipleSelected, then any other file marked selected in the list remains selected.

Parameters:
pFileList IN: Pointer to file list
attributes IN: Selection attribute
pFilename IN: Pointer to the filename
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK on success.
